To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Myelin can be used to train a deep neural network model on multi-source private data without revealing the training examples, (2) Myelin can achieve a level of performance that is competitive with state-of-the-art deep learning models trained on unencrypted data, (3) Myelin achieves this performance using a single server and without requiring any specialized hardware.

(1) we introduce Myelin (Multi-Source Private Deep learning) a framework for training deep neural networks on multiple sources of data in a private manner, (2) we show how Myelin achieves a level of performance on the MNIST dataset that is competitive with non-private training, (3) we show that Myelin is able to learn a model from private data that achieves competitive performance on a real-world task, namely the detection of diabetic retinopathy, and (4) we

Myelin is the first framework that can perform fully private training of deep learning models on a large dataset (MNIST), that Myelin is able to train models that achieve 98.7% accuracy, and that Myelin can train models on a dataset with 10 million samples in 10 minutes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problem: Given a collection of private datasets, how can we train a machine learning system that achieves high accuracy and generalizability, while protecting the privacy of the individual data owners?
the following problem: How can we efficiently train a machine-learning model without revealing the underlying training data?

the following problem: How can we train a machine learning system in a distributed manner without compromising the privacy of the individual data providers, while still achieving a high level of performance?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Myelin framework can be used for training deep neural networks in a fully private manner with minimal accuracy loss.
Myelin is a deep learning framework that combines privacy-preservation primitives to establish a baseline performance for fully private learning.
our work demonstrates that Myelin, a novel deep learning framework, is capable of efficiently training machine learning models on private data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Myelin is a deep learning framework that can train on private data without leaking the data.
we have developed the first fully private deep learning framework, which allows multiple parties to jointly train a deep neural network on private data.
we have built a framework that can be used for training deep learning models in a privacy-preserving way.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite the overheads of privacy-preserving primitives, it is possible to train deep learning models on private data with a small amount of trusted data, and achieve a level of performance which is comparable to the state of the art.
privacy-preserving computation can support large, complex machine learning models.
privacy-preserving machine learning is not a panacea for the data silos that exist today, and that there are fundamental limits to the performance we can expect from such systems.
